newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels claim Mobutu orders massacre of expatriates.
newsitem.headline: Rebels claim Mobutu orders massacre of expatriates.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila has accused President Mobutu Sese Seko through an aide of ordering the massacre of all expatriates in Kinshasa to provoke foreign intervention and avert his downfall.

In a bombshell statement to reporters in Lubumbashi, which was virtually guaranteed to cause panic in Kinshasa, a city of five million, Kabila sent the man he wants to be finance minister to warn that the alleged plot could "start at any minute".

"The AFDL (rebel alliance) has learned from very reliable sources that Mobutu and his team have charged his SARM (military intelligence) and DSP (presidential guard) to kill all the expatriates who live in Kinshasa," Mwana Nanga Mawanpanga said.

"In this way, they could put those killings on our forces which have not reached Kinshasa yet. And the reason for that is that they want to attract the intervention of foreign forces which are in Brazzaville (across the Zaire river in the Congo republic)," he added.
It was not clear whether the rebels' real intent was to provoke the quick evacuation of foreign nationals from Kinshasa before any risk of their being caught up in fighting.

"Instead of invading our country under the pretext of evacuating citizens all they have to do is making Mobutu get out like they did with (Philippines dictator Ferdinand) Marcos, like they did with (Haitian strongman Raoul) Cedras," Mawanpanga said.

More than 1,000 United States, French and Belgian marines are camped in Brazzaville ready to evacuate foreign nationals if Kinshasa looks like becoming the final battleground of Zaire's seven-month-old civil war.

The reason for Thursday evening's suprise announcement, made at short notice in a bizarre news conference by the hotel poolside in Lubumbashi, was not clear. It was unquestionably the authorised word of Kabila, but seemed self-contradictory.

"This was a statement given me by the president (Kabila) himself. He doesn't joke. We have intelligence sources and friends everywhere and we know this plan will soon be executed in Kinshasa," Mawanpanga said.

Referring to one of the most grisly episodes in Zaire's history, he said Mobutu was preparing a repeat of the 1978 Kolwezi massacre in which some 2,000 Europeans were slaughtered during the suppression of an uprising in Katanga (now Shaba) province.
The massacre triggered French military intervention.

Asked if the rebel claim would not provoke panic and evauction, Mawanpanga said: "If they leave Kinshasa peacefully and safely without any foreign intervention we have no problem with that. What we don't want if foreign intervention on our territory.

"But I am sure that if Mobutu's plot succeeds there will be foreign forces in Kinshasa under the pretext of evacuating the citizens, and we don't like that. What they should do is put pressure on Mobutu not to execute his plan.
Western powers such as the U.S. and France and all western powers which used to support Mobutu, cannot prevent Mobutu from doing so without military intervention, he said.
"We want to call the world community's attention... they should understand that if such a thing should happen it is a plot which has been prepared by Mobutu's forces."

"They are ready to act. They could start at any minute. So we want to warn the world community that if such a thing should happen as happened in Kolwezi in 1978, when Mobutu's forces killed all the French in order to attract french intervention, the world community should understand it's a plot, it's not our forces" Mawanpanga said.

"What we are negotiating is Mobutu's peaceful exit from power to save violence and killing of our people. Keep in mind we are liberators...if we can get into Kinshasa peacefully without firing a single shot, that would be the better.
"What we are negotiating with Mobutu is his exit from power. Nothing else. And we will negotiate any time, at any minute."
